text: What is a token in a large language model, and why does the context window size matter in practice?
expected_points: text is split into subword tokens
context window limits input plus output tokens
cost and latency scale with tokens
long inputs must be truncated or chunked
followup: How would you handle a document that is larger than the model's context window?
ideal_answer_hint: Tokens are subword units; the window bounds prompt + completion, driving truncation, chunking, cost and latency.

text: Explain what temperature and top-p control during text generation.
expected_points: top-p restricts sampling to a probability mass
followup: Which settings would you use for structured JSON extraction, and why?
ideal_answer_hint: Both shape sampling; low temperature/top-p for factual or structured output, higher for creative variety.

text: What is the difference between a base (pretrained) model and an instruction-tuned chat model?
expected_points: base model predicts next tokens on raw text
preference tuning such as RLHF or DPO
chat models follow instructions and formats
followup: When might you still choose a base model?
ideal_answer_hint: Base models continue text; instruction/preference tuning teaches them to follow instructions and dialogue formats.

text: Explain self-attention in a transformer and why its cost grows with sequence length.
expected_points: attention weights from scaled dot products
followup: How does a KV cache change inference cost during generation?
ideal_answer_hint: Each token attends to all others via QK^T softmax V, giving O(n^2) compute/memory; KV cache avoids recomputation when decoding.

text: Your LLM feature confidently returns wrong facts. What causes hallucinations and how would you reduce them in production?
expected_points: models generate plausible tokens not verified facts
followup: How would you measure whether your mitigation actually worked?
ideal_answer_hint: Hallucinations come from likelihood-driven generation; mitigate with RAG grounding, citations, refusal paths and measured faithfulness.

text: Compare using a hosted LLM API with self-hosting an open-weight model.
expected_points: cost model per token versus infrastructure
followup: At what usage level would self-hosting start to make financial sense?
ideal_answer_hint: Trade off per-token cost, privacy, latency control and quality against GPU cost and operational complexity.

text: Design an LLM serving setup that handles bursty traffic with a p95 latency budget of two seconds.
followup: Which metrics would you alert on first?
ideal_answer_hint: Use continuous batching, streaming, queue-aware autoscaling with headroom, caching and degraded fallbacks under load.

text: Your monthly LLM bill tripled after launch. How do you cut cost without degrading quality?
expected_points: measure cost per request and per feature
followup: How would you prove quality did not regress?
ideal_answer_hint: Attribute spend, trim context, cache, route easy requests to smaller models, and gate changes on an evaluation set.

text: What are the trade-offs of quantizing a model to 8-bit or 4-bit for inference?
followup: How would you detect a quality drop caused by quantization?
ideal_answer_hint: Quantization saves memory and speeds inference but can degrade accuracy; verify on task evals and hardware support.

text: What is the difference between zero-shot and few-shot prompting?
followup: How do you choose good few-shot examples?
ideal_answer_hint: Few-shot adds input/output examples for in-context learning; it improves format adherence at token cost.

text: What is a system prompt, and what should you put in it?
followup: What should never be placed in a system prompt?
ideal_answer_hint: The system prompt defines role, rules and output format; it must not contain secrets.

text: How would you make an LLM reliably return valid JSON that your code can parse?
followup: What do you do when validation still fails after retries?
ideal_answer_hint: Specify a schema, use structured output features, validate with a schema library and retry or fall back.

text: What is prompt injection, and how would you defend a RAG application against it?
followup: How would you test your defenses?
ideal_answer_hint: Injected instructions in user or retrieved text hijack the model; isolate data, limit tool permissions, filter outputs and red-team.

text: When does chain-of-thought or step-by-step reasoning help, and what are its costs?
expected_points: can be hidden from end users
followup: Would you show the reasoning to end users? Why?
ideal_answer_hint: It helps on multi-step problems but adds tokens and latency, and the stated reasoning is not guaranteed faithful.

text: How do you version and test prompts as they change over time?
followup: What would trigger a prompt rollback?
ideal_answer_hint: Treat prompts as code: version them, pin models and gate changes on a regression evaluation set.

text: Design a prompt management system for a team with many LLM features in production.
followup: How do you keep prompt changes from silently breaking downstream parsers?
ideal_answer_hint: Versioned registry, schema contracts, CI evaluation gates, gradual rollout and per-version metrics.

text: A prompt works with one model but degrades when you switch providers. How do you approach portability?
followup: How would you decide which model a request should go to?
ideal_answer_hint: Abstract the provider, keep per-model prompt variants, rely on structured outputs and evaluate every model change.

text: When should a team stop iterating on prompts and consider fine-tuning or a different architecture instead?
expected_points: need for consistent style or format
latency or cost limits from long prompts
followup: What evidence would you collect before making that call?
ideal_answer_hint: Move on when evals plateau, prompts become too long or costly, and enough labeled data exists to justify training.

text: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation and what problem does it solve?
expected_points: grounds answers in current or private data
followup: How would you improve retrieval quality?
ideal_answer_hint: RAG retrieves relevant context and adds it to the prompt so answers are grounded in up-to-date or private data.

text: What is chunking in a RAG pipeline, and why does chunk size matter?
followup: How would you pick a chunk size for technical documentation?
ideal_answer_hint: Chunks trade precision for context; tune size and overlap per corpus and measure retrieval quality.

text: Walk through the indexing and query steps of a basic RAG pipeline.
expected_points: embed the query and retrieve top-k
followup: Where would you add metadata filtering?
ideal_answer_hint: Index: load, chunk, embed, store. Query: embed, retrieve top-k, build prompt, generate.

text: Users say your RAG answers are often wrong. How do you tell whether retrieval or generation is the problem?
expected_points: retrieval metrics like recall and precision
faithfulness of the answer to context
followup: Which metric would you track first, and why?
ideal_answer_hint: Separate the stages: measure context recall/precision for retrieval and faithfulness for generation on a labeled set.

text: Compare dense, sparse (BM25) and hybrid retrieval.
followup: When does BM25 beat embeddings?
ideal_answer_hint: Dense handles paraphrase, BM25 handles exact terms and identifiers; hybrid with rank fusion usually wins.

text: What is reranking in RAG, and when is it worth the extra latency?
expected_points: cross-encoder scores query and passage together
followup: How many candidates would you rerank?
ideal_answer_hint: A cross-encoder rescores retrieved candidates for better top-k precision at extra latency.

text: Design a RAG system over a million documents that change daily and have per-user access permissions.
followup: How do you make sure a deleted document never appears in answers?
ideal_answer_hint: Incremental ingestion with change detection, ACL metadata filters at query time, deletion propagation and continuous evaluation.

text: Multi-hop questions fail in your RAG system. How would you redesign it?
followup: How would you bound latency in an iterative design?
ideal_answer_hint: Decompose questions, retrieve iteratively or use structured/graph sources, and evaluate on multi-hop cases.

text: When would you choose long-context prompting over RAG, and when not?
expected_points: small stable corpora fit in context
cost and latency of long prompts
RAG for large or changing data
followup: Can the two be combined?
ideal_answer_hint: Long context suits small bounded corpora; RAG scales to large, changing data at lower cost per request.

text: How do vector databases support semantic search?
followup: Which similarity metric would you use for normalized embeddings?
ideal_answer_hint: Text is embedded into vectors; the database returns nearest neighbors by a similarity metric.

text: Compare cosine similarity, dot product and Euclidean distance for embeddings.
followup: Why do many embedding models output normalized vectors?
ideal_answer_hint: With normalized vectors all three give the same ranking; otherwise magnitude changes dot product and distance.

text: What is metadata filtering in a vector store, and why is it useful?
expected_points: filter by category, date or owner
followup: What is the difference between pre-filtering and post-filtering?
ideal_answer_hint: Metadata filters restrict results by attributes, improving relevance and enforcing permissions.

text: How does approximate nearest neighbor search such as HNSW work, and what are its trade-offs?
followup: Which parameters would you tune to improve recall?
ideal_answer_hint: HNSW navigates a layered graph for fast approximate search, trading recall against latency and memory via ef/M.

text: You need to switch to a new embedding model. How do you migrate the vector index safely?
expected_points: vectors from different models are incompatible
build a new index in parallel
followup: How would you minimize downtime during the switch?
ideal_answer_hint: Embeddings are not comparable across models; re-embed into a new index, evaluate, then switch atomically.

text: When would you use a dedicated vector database versus pgvector in an existing PostgreSQL?
followup: What would make you move off pgvector later?
ideal_answer_hint: pgvector keeps one system and transactions; dedicated stores win at large scale or specialized features.

text: Design a multi-tenant vector search service with strict tenant isolation.
followup: How do you prevent one large tenant from hurting others?
ideal_answer_hint: Isolate by namespace or index, enforce tenant filters server-side, apply quotas and test isolation continuously.

text: Your vector search p99 latency is high at 100 million vectors. How do you investigate and fix it?
followup: What recall loss would you accept for lower latency?
ideal_answer_hint: Profile first, then tune index parameters, use vector quantization, shard and replicate, and watch filter selectivity.

text: How would you measure and monitor retrieval quality of a vector index over time?
expected_points: recall at k against exact search
followup: How often would you re-run the evaluation?
ideal_answer_hint: Track recall@k versus exact search on a labeled set, monitor query drift and alert on regressions.

text: What is an LLM agent, and how does it differ from a fixed chain?
followup: What risks does letting the model choose actions introduce?
ideal_answer_hint: A chain runs fixed steps; an agent lets the model choose tools in a loop until it reaches an answer.

text: What is tool or function calling, and how does the application execute a tool?
expected_points: model returns tool name and arguments
result is sent back to the model
followup: How would you validate the arguments the model produces?
ideal_answer_hint: The model emits a structured call; the application validates, executes and returns the result to the model.

text: What is memory in a conversational agent, and what kinds are commonly used?
followup: How would you keep memory within the context window?
ideal_answer_hint: Memory keeps relevant history via buffers, summaries or retrieval from a long-term store within token limits.

text: Explain state, nodes and edges in LangGraph. How would you model the state of an agent?
expected_points: nodes are functions that update state
followup: How would you implement human-in-the-loop approval?
ideal_answer_hint: State is a typed object; nodes return updates; conditional edges pick the next node; checkpoints enable resume.

text: Your agent sometimes loops forever calling the same tool. How do you prevent it?
followup: How would you detect this in production?
ideal_answer_hint: Cap steps, detect repeated calls, return informative tool errors and fall back or escalate.

text: When would you use a ReAct-style agent versus a plan-and-execute design?
followup: How would you recover when a plan step fails?
ideal_answer_hint: ReAct adapts step by step; plan-and-execute is more structured for long tasks but needs replanning on failure.

text: Design a multi-agent system for a complex workflow. How do you coordinate agents and avoid conflicts?
followup: When is a single agent better than many?
ideal_answer_hint: Use an orchestrator with narrow agents, explicit handoff contracts, shared state, tracing and termination rules.

text: How do you secure an agent that can call internal APIs on behalf of users?
followup: Which actions would always require human approval?
ideal_answer_hint: Scope credentials to the user, gate destructive actions, validate all tool I/O and log every call.

text: How would you evaluate an agent, not just its final answers?
followup: How would you build the evaluation dataset?
ideal_answer_hint: Measure task success plus trajectory quality, tool accuracy, cost and steps, using suites built from real traces.

text: Why do teams put LLM applications in Docker containers?
expected_points: same image from dev to production
followup: How would you keep secrets out of the image?
ideal_answer_hint: Containers package code and dependencies for reproducible, portable deployment; secrets come from the runtime.

text: What should you log for each LLM request in production?
expected_points: inputs and outputs with privacy care
followup: What data must you avoid logging?
ideal_answer_hint: Log versions, latency, tokens, errors and feedback while redacting personal or secret data.

text: What is CI/CD, and what checks would you run for an LLM project?
followup: Would you run LLM calls in CI? What are the trade-offs?
ideal_answer_hint: CI runs lint, types, tests and eval regressions on every change; CD deploys passing builds automatically.

text: How would you monitor an LLM application for quality drift after deployment?
followup: What would you do when an alert fires?
ideal_answer_hint: Combine feedback signals, sampled LLM or human evaluation and input drift detection with alerting.

text: How do you safely roll out a new model or prompt version?
followup: Which metrics decide promotion?
ideal_answer_hint: Gate on offline evals, then canary or shadow traffic, compare key metrics and keep instant rollback.

text: An upstream LLM provider has an outage. How should your application behave?
followup: How would you test the fallback path?
ideal_answer_hint: Use timeouts, bounded retries, circuit breakers and a fallback model, degrading gracefully instead of failing.

text: Design an end-to-end LLMOps platform for several product teams.
followup: What would you build first, and why?
ideal_answer_hint: Central gateway with auth, routing and cost tracking, versioned prompts/datasets, eval pipelines and tracing.

text: How would you handle personal data and compliance such as GDPR in an LLM product?
followup: How do you handle a deletion request when data is in a vector index?
ideal_answer_hint: Minimize and redact PII, choose providers with suitable retention, support deletion across stores and audit access.

text: Which SLOs would you define for an LLM-backed service, and how would you measure them?
followup: How do you handle a quality SLO, not just latency?
ideal_answer_hint: Define availability, p95 latency and a measured quality metric with error budgets that gate releases.

text: Why is evaluating LLM outputs harder than evaluating a classifier?
followup: What simple metric could you start with?
ideal_answer_hint: Generated text has many valid forms, so exact accuracy fails; you need rubrics, references or judges.

text: What is LLM-as-a-judge, and what are its limitations?
expected_points: a model scores outputs with a rubric
followup: How would you check whether the judge can be trusted?
ideal_answer_hint: A model grades outputs by rubric; it scales but has biases and must be calibrated against human labels.

text: What is a golden or reference test set, and why do you need one?
followup: How large should it be at the start?
ideal_answer_hint: A fixed curated set of inputs and expected outputs enables repeatable comparisons and catches regressions.

text: Explain faithfulness, answer relevancy and context precision for RAG evaluation.
expected_points: context precision: relevant chunks ranked high
followup: Which one would catch hallucinations?
ideal_answer_hint: Faithfulness checks grounding, relevancy checks focus, context precision checks retrieval ranking.

text: How do you measure agreement between human raters and between humans and an LLM judge?
expected_points: Pearson or Spearman correlation for scores
followup: What would you do if humans disagree with each other?
ideal_answer_hint: Use kappa for chance-corrected agreement and correlation for scores; establish human reliability first.

text: How would you set up offline evaluation so that prompt changes cannot silently regress quality?
followup: How do you keep the dataset from going stale?
ideal_answer_hint: Run a fixed dataset with automated metrics in CI and block merges that fall below thresholds.

text: Design an evaluation framework for an LLM product that covers offline and online quality.
followup: How do offline and online results feed back into each other?
ideal_answer_hint: Combine offline suites as release gates with online A/B metrics, feedback and sampled human review.

text: Your LLM judge and your human raters disagree on 30% of cases. What do you do?
followup: When would you stop trusting the judge entirely?
ideal_answer_hint: Classify disagreements, refine the rubric and judge prompt or model, and re-measure agreement before relying on it.

text: How do you decide whether a measured improvement in your evaluation is real?
followup: How many evaluation samples would you need?
ideal_answer_hint: Account for variance and nondeterminism with repeated runs, confidence intervals and adequate sample sizes.

text: What is fine-tuning, and when should you use it instead of prompting or RAG?
followup: Can fine-tuning add new factual knowledge reliably?
ideal_answer_hint: Fine-tuning adapts behavior and format; use RAG for changing knowledge and try prompting first.

text: What does a supervised fine-tuning dataset look like?
followup: How would you clean noisy examples?
ideal_answer_hint: Pairs of prompts and ideal responses in a consistent chat format, deduplicated and split for validation.

text: What is overfitting in fine-tuning, and how do you detect it?
followup: Which hyperparameters help reduce overfitting?
ideal_answer_hint: Watch validation loss and held-out evals; stop early, reduce epochs or add data.

text: Explain how LoRA works and why it is cheaper than full fine-tuning.
followup: How would you choose the rank?
ideal_answer_hint: LoRA freezes weights and learns low-rank updates, cutting memory and storage while allowing swappable adapters.

text: What is QLoRA, and what are the trade-offs compared with LoRA?
expected_points: fits larger models on smaller GPUs
slower training and small quality risk
followup: Which GPU would you need for a 7B model with QLoRA?
ideal_answer_hint: QLoRA trains LoRA adapters on a 4-bit base model, saving memory at some speed and small quality cost.

text: How would you evaluate a fine-tuned model against the base model?
followup: What is catastrophic forgetting, and how do you check for it?
ideal_answer_hint: Compare both on the same held-out task set plus general benchmarks to catch regressions.

text: Design a pipeline that continuously improves a model from production feedback.
followup: How do you avoid training on bad or adversarial feedback?
ideal_answer_hint: Build a data flywheel with filtered, labeled feedback, scheduled training, eval gates and versioned rollouts.

text: Compare RLHF and DPO for aligning a model with preferences.
expected_points: RLHF trains a reward model and uses RL
followup: When would you still choose RLHF?
ideal_answer_hint: RLHF needs a reward model and RL; DPO optimizes preferences directly, which is simpler and more stable.

text: Your fine-tuned model scores better on your test set but users complain. What went wrong, and how do you fix it?
expected_points: metric does not match user value
followup: How would you rebuild the evaluation set?
ideal_answer_hint: Check for leakage, unrepresentative tests and metric mismatch; rebuild evals from real usage and recheck general skills.
